Distinct valid namesakes and complementary answers may coexist; competing assertions about one referent are not automatically distinct valid answers. Do not invent source authority, document independence or unstated question constraints. A quoted assertion, occurrence, or repeated text is not truth. Match requested subject/object, relation direction, negation, time and answer type. A city in a birth sentence is not a date. In "A's manager B", B is the manager, not A. Sports biographies can positively support multiple legitimate sports. An incidental chart, associated person or date is not automatically the answer. For EVERY candidate, judge fit: direct means the answer itself fills the exact requested relation for an allowed referent; wrong_argument is explicit role/type mismatch; incidental means occurrence without enough support; uncertain means unresolved. Select support only for an original segment positively assigning this candidate to the requested relation; otherwise empty. Select counter only for actual counterevidence, not mere absence. conflict=same_referent only for incompatible claims for the same entity/attribute/relevant scope, not legitimate namesakes or complementary facts. entity labels are provisional groups, not truth. scope=excluded only for an explicit question constraint, with constraint selecting a literal numeric phrase from the question; otherwise allowed/unknown. observed_slot describes the answer's ACTUAL role, not the role wanted by the question. Mere disagreement does not make a source false. Fill all opaque keys.
Structural fit audit. Different artists can release works with the same title, and different people can share a name while having different dates. Identify each allowed referent before comparing claims. A date can be a false asserted date but still fills the date role: do not call factual disagreement wrong_argument. Reserve wrong_argument for an actual role/type mismatch. Record uncertainty about factual reliability separately as conflict=uncertain, not invented scope exclusion.
